title: Fourteen Tasks Under Workspace Ablation
takeaway: With the J-space suppressed, Sonnet 4.5 still classifies, judges, and extracts at close to its normal level, but tasks that require recalling or generating content grounded in silently inferred context collapse, most of them to well below an unablated smaller model. Writing out chain-of-thought largely protects arithmetic from the ablation, consistent with the workspace being where unwritten intermediate steps would otherwise be held.
walkthrough:
The chart covers the paper's [[ablation-task-battery]]: fourteen tasks arranged left to right, four bars each. In the web paper it is drawn live from the underlying scores rather than shipped as an image, and the wide chart scrolls sideways on a narrow screen.

Every bar is a task score divided by the score of an unmodified Sonnet 4.5, one of the [[claude-model-family]], on the same task. A bar at 1.0 means the intervention cost nothing. The gray hatched bar is an unmodified Haiku 4.5, a smaller model, included as a yardstick: a bar below it marks damage worse than dropping a whole model tier. The three orange bars show [[j-space-ablation]] at the three [[ablation-strengths]]. At each token position, across a band of layers, the ten most active [[j-lens-vector]]s are found and the [[residual-stream]]'s projection onto each is zeroed. The strengths differ only in the band: layers 62–71 for light, 54–79 for medium, 42–88 for heavy, in the paper's [[layer-percentage-indexing]]. Tokens in the clean model's top-10 predictions are never ablated, so the intervention aims at internal content rather than at words the model was about to emit. Error bars are [[wilson-interval]]s.

One control anchors the reading. Ablating random directions over the medium layer band leaves two-hop accuracy at 98 percent, the clean model's own score, and [[pretraining-top-1-match]] at 96 percent. The damage below is therefore specific to the J-space, not to perturbation of that magnitude.

Three brackets group the tasks. The left five, MMLU through CoLA, survive even heavy ablation at 0.89–0.96. The right seven, which require recall or free-form generation grounded in inferred content, collapse: under heavy ablation, sonnet writing reaches 0.0, translation 0.02, and the 50-prompt [[multihop-benchmark]] 0.21, all far below unablated Haiku's 0.82–0.85 on the same three tasks. In the middle sit two versions of GSM8K. Solved with [[chain-of-thought]], it holds 0.74 under heavy ablation; answered directly, it falls to 0.54. The paper reads this gap as [[cot-externalization]]: the written steps carry what the workspace would otherwise hold.

The dissociation is the point. With the [[j-space]] suppressed, the model still parses, classifies, and extracts, but it loses the ability to assemble abstract characterizations of context and to generate from them. This is the paper's [[flexible-vs-automatic-dissociation]], tested at full breadth.

terms.definition: The y-axis: each condition's task score divided by unablated Sonnet 4.5's score on that task, so 1.0 means no loss relative to the intact model.
The weakest of the three ablation settings: the top-10 J-lens directions are projected out only over layers 62–71 of depth (on the paper's 0–100 layer scale).
The middle setting, ablating over layers 54–79. It is also the layer range at which the random-direction control is run.
The strongest setting, ablating over layers 42–88, covering most of the workspace band of the model's depth.

Unablated Haiku 4.5, a smaller model from the same family, scored on the same tasks and normalized the same way. It serves as a reference: ablated bars below it mean the ablation cost more than an entire model-size tier.
The subject model of the experiment; all ablations are applied to it, and all bars are normalized to its unablated score.

The intervention behind the orange bars: at each token position, across the given layer band, the residual stream's projections onto the ten most active J-lens vectors are zeroed, sparing any token in the clean model's top-10 next-token predictions.
A standard multiple-choice knowledge benchmark (Hendrycks et al. 2021); here a representative of shallow classification, nearly untouched by ablation.
A task constructed for this paper: picking which item in a set does not belong. A shallow comparison task that survives ablation.
Extractive question answering on SQuAD (Rajpurkar et al. 2016): the answer is a span copied from the given passage. Listed in the data as reading_span; robust to ablation.
A sentiment-labeling task constructed for this paper; a shallow classification that survives ablation.
Judging whether a sentence is grammatically acceptable, from the CoLA benchmark (Warstadt et al. 2019); robust to ablation.
Grade-school math problems (Cobbe et al. 2021) answered with explicit written chain-of-thought. Markedly more robust to ablation than the same problems answered directly.
The same math problems answered directly, without written reasoning, so intermediate steps must be carried internally. Substantially more damaged by ablation than the CoT version.
Decoding Caesar-cipher text, a task constructed for this paper; requires generating content from an inferred transformation and is heavily damaged by ablation.
Completing analogies, constructed for this paper; requires producing a term from an inferred relation and degrades under medium and heavy ablation.
Free-form summarization (TL;DR-style data, Stiennon et al. 2020 / Völske et al. 2017); generation grounded in an assembled understanding of the text, heavily damaged.
Open-domain factual recall (Joshi et al. 2017); recall of facts not present in the prompt, heavily damaged by ablation.

The paper's 50-prompt two-hop factual questions, which need a silently computed bridging entity. Near-ceiling clean, near zero under heavy ablation; the positive control that ablation removes what earlier sections showed the J-space to carry.
A translation task constructed for this paper; free-form generation in another language, almost entirely destroyed by heavy ablation.
Writing a sonnet, constructed for this paper; the most damaged task, scoring zero under heavy ablation.
Asymmetric intervals around each bar; the paper uses Wilson 95 percent intervals for its success-rate error bars.

Three labeled brackets under the x-axis: 'Classification and extractive tasks are robust to workspace ablation' (first five tasks), 'Chain of thought reduces workspace dependence' (the two GSM8K bars), and 'Recall and freeform generation are most damaged by ablation' (last seven tasks).
One direction per vocabulary token per layer, encoding the model's disposition to say that token; the ablation targets the ten most strongly activated of these at each position.

A matched control from the companion strength table (Figure 22): ablating random directions over the medium layer range leaves multihop accuracy at 98 percent and pretraining top-1 match at 96 percent, showing the damage is specific to J-space directions.

numbers.meaning: Tasks in the battery. Six (sentiment, analogy, odd one out, Caesar cipher, translation, sonnet writing) were constructed for this work; the rest are standard benchmarks, plus the paper's own 50-prompt multihop set.
J-lens vectors ablated per token position: the k most strongly activated directions whose residual-stream projections are zeroed, excluding tokens in the clean forward pass's top-10 predictions.
The layer bands (on the paper's 0–100 percent-of-depth scale) over which light, medium, and heavy ablation are applied; the strengths differ in nothing else.
The normalization point: unablated Sonnet 4.5's own score on each task. Bars at or near 1.0 mean the ablation cost nothing on that task.
Heavy-ablation scores across the five classification and extraction tasks (MMLU 0.949, odd one out 0.920, SQuAD 0.928, sentiment 0.964, CoLA 0.892): essentially intact even at the strongest setting.
Heavy-ablation scores on sonnet writing, translation, and multihop reasoning: the near-total collapse of generation and inference tasks.
Heavy-ablation scores on TriviaQA, summarization, Caesar decoding, and analogy completion: the rest of the recall-and-generation group, all far below the Haiku reference.

GSM8K under heavy ablation with chain-of-thought (0.740) versus answered directly (0.539): written-out steps substantially shield the task, read as externalizing what the workspace would otherwise carry.
GSM8K without CoT under light ablation, lower than under medium ablation (0.864). The data are non-monotonic on this one task; the paper does not comment on it.

Unablated Haiku 4.5's normalized scores on the seven damaged tasks (Caesar 0.783, multihop 0.816, translation 0.845, sonnet writing 0.853, summarization 0.862, TriviaQA 0.868, analogy 0.971): the smaller-model yardstick that medium and heavy ablation fall well below.

The random-direction control at the medium layer band: multihop accuracy (equal to the clean model's 98%) and pretraining top-1 match, showing matched-size perturbation along non-J-space directions is nearly harmless.
Prompts in the multihop reasoning evaluation, reused from the paper's two-hop benchmark.
Token positions of pretraining-like text behind the pretraining top-1 match statistic quoted for the strengths and the control.

Medium ablation on the damaged group spans this range (sonnet writing 0.201, translation 0.348, multihop 0.483, TriviaQA 0.531, analogy 0.665, summarization 0.674, Caesar 0.804): intermediate damage, ordered roughly as under heavy ablation.
Light ablation leaves 13 of 14 tasks at or above roughly this level (minimum outside GSM8K-direct: sonnet writing at 0.799); only direct arithmetic drops sharply at the lightest setting.
